assumptions: THIS INCREMENT LANDS BATCH 120 (publisher.meta) AND ITS CLOSURE 122, under the Product Owner's disposition of 2026-09-15 (evidence/WP-0A-DB-00/product-owner-disposition-2026-09-15-batch-120.md), which answers the fourteen questions in evidence/WP-0A-DB-00/a0-batch-120-plan-2026-09-15.md §11 with the Author's recommended option on every one. Nothing here re-opens any of them.

§8.3 gives this family TWO rows and they do not fall one per table. "Publish now/cancel pending" is the INTENT -- `Y` for the owner and the admin, `P` for the editor with no capability defined anywhere, `N` for the approver and the viewer. "Publish delivery/post/metric INSERT" is everything below it -- `N` in every client column, `S` for the service. So one table of five is client-writable and the other four are refused to every client role at the GRANT layer.

RFC-2026-022 IS APPROVED AND NOT IN EFFECT, so the `S` cell is CLASSIFIED AND NOT ENFORCED: three CARRIED rows in db/foundation/lint/service-policy-map.json for the target, the job and the post, and no policy anywhere. app_worker holds the grants and no policy (batch 010's shape), so its four INSERT refusals are POLICY-layer and flip with the negative control, while its rehome and delete refusals are GRANT-layer and permanent.

THE READINGS THIS BATCH TOOK AND LABELLED AS READINGS, each now an entry in the work package's open_blockers rather than a sentence in a comment: that "delivery" means the target AND the job; that a client may write an intent although RFC-2026-012's inventory line says the family's INSERT is service-only; that §8.4's "Job redacted status SELECT" may or may not govern a publisher job, which the redacted client grant satisfies either way; that one job per send is the right shape although §4.8 states a per-target uniqueness that then becomes moot; and that the editor's undefined `P` is a refusal rather than an explicit-scope grant.

THE RAW PROVIDER IDENTIFIER IS DEFERRED RATHER THAN SOLVED. §9.1 makes an external post ID PROVIDER-3, so app.published_posts stores one sha256 and no permalink. Batch 110 named batch 120 as the batch that would have to give the raw value a home; it does not, because the mechanism §9.3 would need has no decision behind it and the typed service does not exist. The consequence is stated rather than absorbed: nothing can address a Page at the provider until that debt is paid.

security_privacy_cost_impact: SUBSTANTIAL AND THE WHOLE POINT OF THE BATCH. Five new tenant tables, every one ENABLE + FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, each with one SELECT policy on active membership and one RESTRICTIVE narrowing resolving through the intent and then through app.content_items -- four links from the row to the Page override that decides it. §9.1's PROVIDER-3 columns are withheld from the client per column and asserted against the live ACL: external_post_hash, provider_request_key, last_error_code, kernel_job_id. NO RAW PROVIDER IDENTIFIER AND NO PERMALINK EXISTS ANYWHERE IN THE SCHEMA -- batch 110 named this batch as the one that would have to give the raw external identifier a home and it defers to the typed service in writing, with the consequence stated. app_worker holds grants and NO POLICY on the four service-written tables (RFC-2026-022 approved and NOT IN EFFECT), so every service refusal is attributable to row level security rather than to a forgotten GRANT. Cost: none beyond storage; no provider call, no credential, no network.
migration_and_data_impact: TWO MIGRATIONS AND ONE FORWARD KEY ON A MERGED TABLE. 120_publisher.sql creates five tables, fourteen indexes, three set_updated_at triggers, ten policies and the grants, and ADDS (never rewrites -- migration invariant 1) one unique key to batch 081's app.content_targets: content_targets_destination_key (workspace_id, business_profile_id, id, social_account_id), which is what lets a send name an aim AND the account it resolves to in one key. That is batch 111's precedent on batch 110's table. 122_publisher_service_path_closed.sql creates two RESTRICTIVE policies and no object. NO DATA IS MIGRATED and no instance is provisioned: the migration set has never been applied to any database this repository owns, so there is no deployed schema to change. tests/db/identity/fixtures/081-content-targets-fixture.sql now writes its six rows with ids fixed from the catalog rather than defaulting, which changes no row's content. Forward fix only; no down migration exists and none will.
compatibility_impact: The isolation suite grows 857 -> 941 cases and the static suite 647 -> 658 tests; three declared floors are RAISED and none lowered. .github/workflows/ci.yml gains five negative-control entries, so the CI job does five more suite runs. The fixture catalog gains twelve symbols and overturns batch 081's "no symbol for a content target" declaration with a stated third clause. No contract in contract-catalog/ changes; no public interface exists yet to break.
known_limitations: NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY CAN PUBLISH ANYTHING, and that is the design followed rather than a limitation of the batch: §8.3 marks the delivery, the post and the metric `S`, RFC-2026-022 §5/8 measures that the only member of app_worker is postgres (which bypasses RLS), and no command function exists anywhere (RFC-2026-021 §10).

AND THE SERVICE COULD NOT COMPOSE THE STATEMENT EVEN IF A POLICY ADMITTED IT. Measured live: app_worker is refused app.content_targets and app.content_variants outright, and a send COPIES an aim and a variant from those two tables. New open blocker; it is also why two case ids hold their ids as parameters rather than resolving them by subselect.

§4 invariant 5's two conditions -- a pinned asset version `ready` with rights valid -- are enforced by nothing on app.publish_target_assets, which is blocker 153's finding about app.content_asset_links on a second table.
app.publish_intents carries no `status` column (the Owner's question 5b), so "cancel PENDING" is not a database rule: a cancellation is accepted whatever the sends already did.

Nothing holds a variant's platform (`facebook`/`instagram`) to its destination's account_kind (`fb`/`ig`) or to its post's platform; the fixture keeps them consistent by hand so no case demonstrates the gap as though it were a feature.
Batch 091 does not exist; `request_kind = 'scheduled'` may be declared with no schedule row anywhere and nothing refuses the combination.
open_risks_or_blockers: TEN opened by this increment (work-packages/WP-0A-DB-00.json open_blockers, 164 -> 174). The one a reader should meet first: THE SERVICE CANNOT PERFORM THE FAN-OUT §8.3 MARKS `S` FOR IT, because app_worker holds no grant on app.content_targets or app.content_variants and a send copies from both -- measured, not reasoned. Then: which §8 row governs a publisher job; the client INSERT on the intent departing from RFC-2026-012's inventory line (the Owner's question 14); no `status` on the intent; two vocabularies for one distinction; no soft lifecycle on three mutable tables; one job per send as a reading that makes §4.8's own uniqueness rule moot; §4 invariant 5 unenforced on the pin; batch 091 absent; and the editor's undefined publishing capability, which the Owner disposed as a refusal (question 2).
rollback_or_forward_fix: Revert through a reviewed revert PR: the two migrations, the five tables and the forward key on app.content_targets go, the isolation suite returns to 857 cases and the static suite to 647 tests, the three floors return to their previous numbers, the five ci.yml entries go, and the twelve fixture symbols and batch 081's six fixed ids revert with them. No database has ever received the migration set -- no instance is provisioned -- so there is no deployed schema to roll back and no data to restore. A defect found after merge is corrected by a forward batch, never by rewriting 120 or 122 (migration invariant 1).
